title: Add readonly support to all input types, including radio, checkbox, and select

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

### Summary

Currently, the `readonly` attribute is only supported on free-text input types (`text`, `number`, `email`, etc.) and `textarea`. However, many real-world use cases require developers to display preselected values in inputs like `select`, `radio`, or `checkbox`, in a way that:

- Prevents user interaction (non-editable),
- Still includes the value in form submission,
- Does not suggest (visually or semantically) that the field is excluded from submission, as `disabled` does.

The current limitation forces developers to use workarounds (e.g., using `disabled` plus a hidden field), which are semantically misleading and can confuse users.

---

### Use Case

Imagine a form that displays user information for editing. Some values are selected from a predefined list (e.g., organization, team, user access level, desk number) but should not be editable depending on the user's rights. These values should be:

- Displayed using native UI controls (e.g., `<select>`, `<input type="radio">`, `<input type="checkbox">`)
- Not modifiable by the user
- Still submitted as part of the form data

Currently, `readonly` is not allowed on these input types. Using `disabled` works visually but prevents data submission, requiring a hidden input — this creates a semantic and UX inconsistency.

For this kind of use case, various workarounds can be implemented successfully. However, the same workarounds could also be applied to text inputs — which already support `readonly`. In other words, there is no technical or conceptual reason why `readonly` should be considered appropriate for text-based inputs but not for selection-based ones.

---

### Proposed Change

Extend support of the `readonly` attribute to the following elements:

- `<select>`
- `<input type="radio">`
- `<input type="checkbox">`

This would:
- Allow developers to clearly express intent: “this value is part of the form but cannot be changed”
- Improve semantic consistency across all input types
- Reduce reliance on visually misleading or technically convoluted workarounds

---

### Why This Matters

- The distinction between `readonly` and `disabled` is already clear and useful for text inputs.
- The same logic can and should apply to selection-based inputs.
- It improves both **developer ergonomics** and **user experience clarity**.

Thank you for considering this!
